verses.text: Joseph went and told Pharaoh, "My father and brothers have come from the land of Canaan, with their flocks and herds and everything they own. They are now in Goshen."
He chose five of his brothers and presented them to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked the brothers, "What is your work?" "Your servants are shepherds," they replied to Pharaoh, "just as our ancestors were."

They also said to him, "We have come to live here for a while, because the famine is terrible in Canaan and there is no grass for your servants' flocks. So now, please let your servants settle in Goshen."
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you,

and the land of Egypt is open to you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land. Let them live in Goshen. And if you know of any among them who are especially skilled, put them in charge of my own livestock."
Then Joseph brought his father Jacob in and presented him to Pharaoh. And Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked him, "How old are you?"
Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The years of my travels are a hundred and thirty. My years have been few and hard, and they do not equal the years of the travels of my ancestors."
Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and left his presence.
So Joseph settled his father and his brothers in Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had ordered.
Joseph also provided his father and his brothers and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their children.
But there was no food anywhere in the land, because the famine was so terrible. The people of Egypt and Canaan were weak with hunger because of the famine.
Joseph collected all the money that could be found in Egypt and Canaan in payment for the grain they were buying, and he brought it to Pharaoh's palace.
When the money of the people of Egypt and Canaan was all gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, "Give us food. Why should we die in front of your eyes? Our money is all used up."
"Then bring your livestock," Joseph said. "I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock, since your money is all gone."

So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their sheep and goats, their cattle and their donkeys. And he brought them through that year with food in exchange for all their livestock.

When that year was over, they came to him the following year and said, "We cannot hide from our master the fact that our money is gone, and our livestock now belongs to you. There is nothing left for our master except our bodies and our land.

Why should we die in front of your eyes, we and our land as well? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we with our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed so that we can live and not die, and so that the land does not become a desert."
So Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh. The Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields, because the famine was too much for them. The land became Pharaoh's,
and Joseph made the people slaves from one end of Egypt to the other.
But he did not buy the land of the priests, because they received a regular share of food from Pharaoh and had enough to live on from what Pharaoh gave them. That is why they did not sell their land.
Joseph said to the people, "Now that I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh, here is seed for you so that you can plant the ground.
But when the crops come in, give a fifth of them to Pharaoh. The other four-fifths you may keep as seed for the fields and as food for yourselves, your households and your children."
"You have saved our lives," they said. "Please be kind to us, our master, and we will be Pharaoh's slaves."
So Joseph made it a law about land in Egypt, still in force today, that a fifth of the harvest belongs to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests did not become Pharaoh's.
The Israelites settled in Egypt in the region of Goshen. They gained property there and had many children and grew greatly in number.
Jacob lived in Egypt for seventeen years, and he lived a hundred and forty-seven years in all.

When the time came near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, "If you love me, put your hand under my thigh and promise that you will show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt.
When I rest with my ancestors, carry me out of Egypt and bury me where they are buried." "I will do as you say," Joseph said.
"Promise me," Jacob said. Then Joseph promised him, and Israel bowed down in worship as he leaned on the top of his staff.
